resources.string: Set up your own server in a few minutes
Rent a small server (a VPS), then type its address and password here. ZeroNet installs and starts everything on it and gives you the configs to use.
You can also see how many devices are connected to it, live.
Only counts are shown. No address of anyone connected is ever read, kept or sent.
The password is used once to log in and is not kept. The app puts its own key on the server instead.
Fast, and looks like a normal website
Also over REALITY, on its own port. A different traffic shape to try when the first does not connect.
Works through DNS only. Needs your own domain.
A subdomain you own, like t.example.com. The next screens show what to set up.
The address is just the IP, like 203.0.113.7.
The SSH port is a number, usually 22.
Type your tunnel domain, like t.example.com.
Connected. The server says its identity is:
Compare it with the one in your hosting panel (many show it on the server\'s page or console). If it is the same, continue. Nothing secret has been sent yet.
Point your domain at the server
1. Open dash.cloudflare.com, pick your domain, then DNS, Records, Add record.
2. Add these two records. Keep the cloud grey (DNS only), never orange.
You typed a name, not an IP: use the server\'s IP address as the value of the first record.
3. Check it. It can take a few minutes to spread; you can also install now and test later.
Not on Cloudflare? Any registrar works: add the same two records.
The record points at your server. Good.
The name resolves, but not to this server. Check the first record\'s value.
Not visible yet. If you just added it, wait a few minutes and check again.
This takes a minute or two. Keep the app open.
Nothing half-finished is left running. Fix the cause and try again.
QR code of the config link
Added to your servers. You can connect to it now.
Could not add it to your servers.
These files are for the MasterDnsVPN program on a computer. In this app, use the link above.
The files hold the tunnel\'s key: share them only with people you trust.
Port %1$d was already used by %2$s, so port %3$d is used instead.
The ports were opened in the server\'s firewall (%1$s).
Your hosting provider may have its own firewall. If nothing connects, open %1$s in its panel.
The server program was uploaded from this app and was not checked against the signed list.
The app could not log back in with its own key, so it will ask for the password next time.
Counted from the server\'s log: up to 5 minutes behind, with no traffic figure.
MasterDNS did not answer through any public resolver. Check that the two DNS records are right and wait a few minutes.
MasterDNS works: %1$d of %2$d resolvers reached it (best %3$d ms).
Removed. The server is clean again.

It stops and deletes the server program and its settings, closes the ports it opened, and removes this app\'s key from the server. Everything else on the server stays. Configs you gave to people stop working.
Only forget it in this app
Use this when the server is gone or you cannot reach it. Nothing is changed on the server.
Paste the key text (-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----)
Key passphrase (only if it has one)
Use this when the server does not allow passwords. The key is used once to log in and is never saved. Use the private key, not the .pub file.
Paste or choose your private SSH key.
That is not a private key. It should start with -----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----. Did you pick the .pub file?
